unsupported_claims: The AI claims the tree can be kept only while frequency estimates remain adequate, and rebuilt when frequencies drift; the evidence says the tree can be built for the maximum cardinality when |V| is known or boundable, not rebuilt on drift.

The AI says new vertices are inserted as new leaves by splitting or attaching near low-frequency nodes; the evidence says vertices are assigned to one of the remaining pre-built leaves when first seen, not inserted into the tree.
The AI says the tree is built from an initial sample and not rebuilt after drift, which is not in the evidence.

The AI says the tree is weighted by visit frequency in the walk corpus; the evidence only mentions Huffman coding for frequent elements in the streaming section, and the core streaming condition (known or boundable cardinality of V) is omitted.
The AI's claim that vertex-frequency distribution known enables the tree is only loosely tied to the source, which says frequency estimation a priori is an optional refinement for assignment.
rationale: The gold answer states the key condition is that the cardinality of V is known or boundable, with new vertices assigned to remaining pre-built leaves on first sight. The AI answer misses this condition and instead describes dynamic leaf insertion and periodic rebuilding, which the evidence does not contain.
